title: 1MBN Myoglobin curated conservation teaching set
classification: straightforward single-protein reference; monomeric sperm-whale myoglobin with heme ligand
teachingQuestion: Which myoglobin residues are conserved across vertebrate oxygen-storage globins, and how do they relate to the heme pocket?

alignment.gapTreatment: Gap columns are included in display; amino-acid conservation scoring excludes gaps from residue-frequency counts.

studentContext.whatIsCompared: Full-length vertebrate myoglobin orthologs, not hemoglobin alpha or beta chains.
studentContext.whySelected: Reviewed UniProt records with compatible length, complete sequences, and useful vertebrate diversity.
studentContext.whatConservationMeans: Similarity within this curated myoglobin teaching set; it is evidence for conserved globin constraints, not proof that every invariant residue has the same function.
studentContext.whatToNotice: Look at proximal/distal heme-pocket residues, conserved histidines, and helix packing positions.
limitations: Eight sequences are enough for teaching but not a full evolutionary-rate model.
Hemoglobin paralogs are excluded to keep the question focused on myoglobin.
